summary: A perception module that detects pedestrians for the emergency braking function of passenger cars, sold to car makers for type approval.
headline: The module is a safety component of a vehicle covered by Annex I, Section B, so it is high-risk under Article 6(1), with only a few provisions of the Act applying directly.

steps.title: Scope
steps.question: Is this an AI system that falls under the Act?
steps.reasoning: The module infers from camera input whether a pedestrian is ahead, so it is an AI system placed on the Union market.

citations.label: Article 3(1)
citations.title: Definitions
citations.quote: ‘AI system’ means a machine-based system that is designed to operate with varying levels of autonomy

steps.title: Prohibited practices
steps.question: Is it a prohibited AI practice under Article 5?
steps.reasoning: Pedestrian detection for braking is not an Article 5 practice.

steps.title: High-risk classification
steps.question: Is it high-risk under Article 6(1) with Annex I or Article 6(2) with Annex III?
steps.reasoning: Motor vehicles are covered by the type-approval legislation listed in Section B of Annex I, and the module is a safety component of the vehicle. Article 2(2) then limits which provisions of the Act apply directly.

citations.label: Article 2(2)
citations.title: Scope
citations.quote: only Article 6(1), Article 60a and Articles 102 to 112 shall apply

steps.title: Article 6(3) exemption
steps.question: Does the Article 6(3) exemption take it out of the high-risk class?
steps.reasoning: The Article 6(3) exemption only concerns Annex III systems.

steps.title: Transparency duties
steps.question: Do the Article 50 transparency obligations apply?
steps.reasoning: The module does not interact with people or generate content.

steps.title: General-purpose AI
steps.question: Is a general-purpose AI model provided, with Chapter V obligations?
steps.reasoning: It is a narrow perception model.

deadlines.label: The AI Act enters into force
deadlines.detail: Article 113: the Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after its publication in the Official Journal (12 July 2024). Entry into force is not the same as application: most rules apply later, see the dates below.

deadlines.label: Prohibited practices and AI literacy apply
deadlines.detail: Article 113, third paragraph, point (a): Chapters I and II (general provisions including Article 4 AI literacy, and the Article 5 prohibitions) apply from 2 February 2025, except Article 5(1), points (ba) and (bb), and Article 5(1a) and (1b), which apply from 2 December 2026. Article 4 in its current wording (support the development of AI literacy) applies since Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 entered into force on 27 July 2026.

deadlines.label: Penalty rules apply
deadlines.detail: Article 113, third paragraph, point (b): Chapter XII (penalties) applies from 2 August 2025. Breaking an Article 5 prohibition can be fined up to EUR 35 000 000 or, if the offender is an undertaking, up to 7 % of total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher (Article 99(3)); breaches of other duties, including Articles 16, 26 and 50, up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3 % (Article 99(4)). For SMEs and start-ups the lower of the two amounts applies (Article 99(6)); for SMCs the lower amount applies to the fines of paragraphs 4 and 5 (Article 99(6a)).

deadlines.label: Digital Omnibus on AI enters into force
deadlines.detail: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 of 8 July 2026, published in the Official Journal on 24 July 2026, enters into force on the third day after publication (its Article 4). From this date Articles 102 to 110 apply (Article 113, third paragraph, point (d)), and the amended provisions that have no later date, such as Article 4 and Article 4a, apply. It moves the high-risk dates, adds two prohibitions from 2 December 2026 and adds a transition period for Article 50(2).

deadlines.label: Amendments to the Section B sectoral acts apply
deadlines.detail: Article 113, third paragraph, point (d): Articles 102 to 110 apply from 27 July 2026. Articles 102 to 109 require the Commission to take the Chapter III, Section 2 requirements into account when adopting delegated or implementing acts under the Section B acts on aviation, vehicles, marine equipment and rail.

deadlines.label: General date of application
deadlines.detail: Article 113, second paragraph: the Regulation applies from 2 August 2026, except where Article 113 sets another date. This includes Chapter IV (Article 50 transparency duties) and Article 101 (fines for general-purpose AI model providers). Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 (high-risk classification, requirements and obligations) no longer apply from this date: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 moved them, see the high-risk entries.

deadlines.label: Transparency duties of Article 50 apply
deadlines.detail: Article 50 is in Chapter IV, which follows the general date of application in Article 113. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 did not move this date; it only added a later date for Article 50(2) marking by systems already on the market (next entry). A high-risk system can carry Article 50 duties as well (Article 50(6)).

deadlines.label: Article 6(1) classification applies to AI in products covered by Annex I Section B
deadlines.detail: Article 113, third paragraph, point (c)(ii) sets 2 August 2028 for Chapter III Sections 1 to 3 as regards Article 6(1) and Annex I. For products under Section B (vehicles, aviation, rail, marine equipment, machinery and the other Section B acts), Article 2(2) says only Article 6(1), Article 60a and Articles 102 to 112 apply, so the high-risk requirements reach these systems through the sectoral acts, not from this date. For machinery, the delegated acts that add the AI requirements to Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 shall apply by 2 August 2028 (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744, Article 3(1)).
